title: Amazing Adventures
note: Split anthology: Inhumans (Kirby) and Black Widow. One of Jack Kirby's last Marvel assignments before he departed for DC.

keys.note: First issue — Inhumans / Black Widow split anthology; Kirby art

title: Astonishing Tales
note: Split book: Ka-Zar (Wally Wood) and Doctor Doom (Larry Lieber). An unusual Bronze Age pairing that never quite found its audience.

keys.note: First issue — Ka-Zar / Doctor Doom split book

title: The Avengers
note: Marvel's flagship super-team, running from Lee/Kirby into Buscema's polished Bronze era. The early #2–41 run is essential. Strong collector demand across the entire run. Three duplicate issues available for trade or sale.

keys.note: King-Size Specials — oversized issues with extra stories and pin-ups

title: Captain Marvel
note: Mar-Vell's early solo title with Gene Colan and Frank Springer art. #17 introduces Carol Danvers, who would go on to become Ms. Marvel and eventually Captain Marvel. Modest but steady collector interest.

title: Captain Savage & Leatherneck Raiders
note: WWII series spun off from Sgt. Fury, following a Marine Raiders unit. Dick Ayers art throughout. Solid war storytelling with modest collector value.

keys.note: First issue — USMC Leatherneck Raiders debut

title: Nick Fury, Agent of SHIELD
note: Jim Steranko's psychedelic spy masterwork. Issues #1–5 are Steranko — some of the most visually innovative comics of any era. A cornerstone of any serious Silver Age Marvel collection.

keys.note: Full Steranko run — highest collector demand in the series

title: Outlaws of the West
note: Late Atlas / early Marvel western anthology. Low circulation title, single issue here. Modest but genuine collector interest in pre-hero Atlas westerns.

title: The Sub-Mariner
note: John Buscema art on Namor's Silver Age solo series. Two issues from a strong early run. Namor comics from this era have consistent demand.

title: Tales to Astonish
note: Sprawling Silver Age anthology that carried Ant-Man, Giant-Man, the Hulk, and Sub-Mariner across its long run. An extraordinary slice of early Marvel history. #47 is prime Ant-Man era; #81+ is core Lee/Kirby Hulk.

title: Where Monsters Dwell
note: Bronze Age monster anthology reprinting classic pre-hero monster stories by Lee and Kirby from the late 1950s. First issue.

keys.note: First issue — reprints classic Kirby/Lee monster stories from the Atlas era

title: Marvel Collectors' Item Classics
note: Prestige reprint anthology collecting the earliest Marvel issues — FF, early Spider-Man, Thor, Iron Man. Condition matters; these were sold and read as cheaply reprinted material.

title: Marvel Comics Group — Black Panther
note: Reprint-era Marvel. Black Panther content from this period has seen growing collector interest following his modern prominence.

title: Marvel Comics Group — Fantastic Four
note: Bronze Age Fantastic Four, #215 in the Marv Wolfman / Keith Pollard era. Solid single issue.

title: Marvel's Greatest Comics
note: Reprint anthology collecting early Fantastic Four and other Marvel classics. An affordable entry point for Silver Age content.

title: Marvel Tales
note: The longest-running Marvel reprint anthology, collecting Amazing Spider-Man from the very beginning. #1 reprints Amazing Fantasy #15 — the most affordable way to own Spider-Man's origin. A 27-issue run is a substantial set.

title: Strange Tales
note: The defining Silver Age anthology: Doctor Strange and Nick Fury sharing one book. #135 is a true cornerstone of Marvel history. The Steranko run (#151–168) is among the most visually innovative comics of any era. Two duplicate issues.

keys.note: Jim Steranko takes over Nick Fury — psychedelic op-art spy stories; landmark run

title: Thor
note: Jack Kirby's cosmic Asgard epics form the spine of this enormous run. The Kirby run (#126–177) is the core; the collection has 18 duplicate issues — an excellent trade or gifting resource. One of the deepest single-character Kirby runs in existence.

keys.note: First issue of Thor solo title — continued from Journey Into Mystery #125

title: Journey Into Mystery
note: The crucible of Silver Age Thor — Kirby at full creative power, supported by Tales of Asgard backup strips. #91–125 is the complete second half of Thor's run in this anthology. Contains some of Marvel's most historically significant individual issues.

title: Tales of Asgard
note: One-shot collection of the Tales of Asgard backup strips from Journey Into Mystery. Pure Jack Kirby mythology — the complete Asgardian saga in one volume.

keys.note: Sole issue — collects all Tales of Asgard backup strips; single printing

title: Sgt. Fury and his Howling Commandos
note: The longest-running WWII comic in Marvel history. Stan Lee and Jack Kirby launched it as a bet that a war comic could sell on character. Dick Ayers art through most of this run. A large, solid set from a beloved title.

keys.note: Earlier issues in the run have higher demand than the later reprint era

title: Sgt. Fury Specials
note: Annual specials reprinting classic Howling Commandos stories. Bronze Age reprint format. One duplicate.

title: Special Marvel Edition
note: Oversized anthology format reprinting early Marvel material in a larger trim size. Single issue.

keys.note: First issue of oversized Marvel anthology format
